keywords.def: situation in which a person feels secure, comfortable, or in control
change to successfully deal with a new situation
basic and important type of food that is regularly eaten by a large portion of the population
be guaranteed to experience a surprising or unpleasant situation
small adjustment to something in order to improve it
way of solving a problem by trying a number of different methods and learning from the mistakes you make

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC学英语的《6 Minute English》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Beth. Every country has its own favourite foods.
sentences.zh: 我是Neil。我是Beth。每个国家都有自己最喜欢的食物。

sentences.en: So, when people leave home and move to a different country, getting used to the new food there can be a surprise.
sentences.zh: 所以，当人们离开家乡搬到另一个国家时，习惯那里的新食物可能会让人大吃一惊。

sentences.en: Food can have strange-sounding names. If you know what a toad is, it's an animal, very similar to a frog, you might be surprised to hear that a famous English meal is 'toad-in-the-hole'.
sentences.zh: 食物可能会有听起来很奇怪的名字。如果你知道什么是toad（蟾蜍），它是一种动物，跟青蛙非常相似，你听到一道著名的英国菜叫“toad-in-the-hole（穴中蟾蜍）”时可能会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Don't worry though, it's made with sausages, not toads!
sentences.zh: 不过别担心，它是用香肠做的，而不是蟾蜍！

sentences.en: In this programme, we're exploring people's first impressions of a new culture through its food.
sentences.zh: 在这个节目中，我们将通过食物来探讨人们对新文化的第一印象。

sentences.en: We'll be hearing how two women, one a refugee, the other a dietitian, adapted to the food of their new home.
sentences.zh: 我们将听到两位女性是如何适应新家园饮食的，其中一位是难民，另一位是营养学家。

sentences.en: And, as usual, we'll be learning some useful new vocabulary too.
sentences.zh: 而且，像往常一样，我们也会学到一些有用的新词汇。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Neil.
sentences.zh: 但首先，Neil，我有一个问题要问你。

sentences.en: A British summer wouldn't be complete without a traditional 'cream tea' – scones, cream, and jam, eaten with a cup of tea.
sentences.zh: 没有传统的“奶油茶点”——烤饼、奶油和果酱，再配上一杯茶，英国的夏天就不算完整。

sentences.en: It sounds lovely, but strangely there have been many arguments over cream teas.
sentences.zh: 听起来很诱人，但奇怪的是，关于奶油茶点的争论一直很多。

sentences.en: So, is the cream tea debate about: a) whether to drink tea or coffee? b) whether to put cream or jam onto the scone first? or, c) whether strawberry or raspberry jam is better?
sentences.zh: 那么，关于奶油茶点的争论是关于：a）是喝茶还是喝咖啡？b）是先抹奶油还是先抹果酱到烤饼上？还是c）草莓果酱还是树莓果酱更好？

sentences.en: Well, I think the controversy is whether to add cream or jam first.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为争论的焦点是先加奶油还是先加果酱。

sentences.en: OK, Neil. I'll reveal the correct answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的，Neil。我稍后会在节目中揭晓正确答案。

sentences.en: Natalia Tkachenko arrived in the Netherlands after leaving her home in Ukraine, following the Russian invasion.
sentences.zh: Natalia Tkachenko在俄罗斯入侵乌克兰后，离开了自己的家乡来到荷兰。

sentences.en: She moved in with Weronika Groszewska, who's originally from Poland, and her family, starting them on a journey to open their own restaurant, Natalia's Kitchen.
sentences.zh: 她和原本来自波兰的Weronika Groszewska及其家人住在一起，这开启了他们开设自己的餐厅“Natalia's Kitchen”的旅程。

sentences.en: Here's Natalia talking with BBC World Service programme, 'The Food Chain':
sentences.zh: 这里是Natalia在接受BBC世界频道节目《The Food Chain》采访时的谈话：

sentences.en: Of course, at first it felt like I am well out of, what they call, my comfort zone.
sentences.zh: 当然，一开始我觉得自己完全超出了他们所说的“舒适区”。

sentences.en: When you stay in a certain environment you get used to it, but when you move to another country where you live and work, you experience difficulties, and you have to adapt to get used to local foods.
sentences.zh: 当你待在某种环境中时你会习以为常，但当你搬到一个生活和工作的新国家时，你会经历困难，你必须适应以习惯当地的食物。

sentences.en: Here, they don't have some of the staples we had in Ukraine, ingredients are different, and so you start working with local foods, find replacements, cook with what you have.
sentences.zh: 在这里，他们没有我们在乌克兰时的一些主食，配料也不同，所以你开始与当地食物打交道，寻找替代品，用你手头有的东西烹饪。

sentences.en: At first, Natalia felt out of her comfort zone, a familiar situation in which someone feels secure and in control.
sentences.zh: 一开始，Natalia感到超出了她的舒适区，这是一种人们感到安全和掌控之中的熟悉状态。

sentences.en: She had to adapt to her new life in the Netherlands, she had to change in order to succeed in her new situation.
sentences.zh: 她必须适应在荷兰的新生活，她必须做出改变以便在新环境中取得成功。

sentences.en: Some of the staple ingredients Natalia used in Ukraine weren't available in the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: Natalia在乌克兰使用的一些主食配料在荷兰买不到。

sentences.en: A staple is a basic and important type of food that is regularly eaten by a large portion of the population.
sentences.zh: 主食是很大一部分人口经常食用的基本且重要的食物类型。

sentences.en: So, Natalia adapted her recipes, replacing Ukrainian with Dutch ingredients to create a new kind of cooking which her customers loved.
sentences.zh: 因此，Natalia调整了她的食谱，用荷兰配料替代了乌克兰配料，创造了一种深受顾客喜爱的新型烹饪。

sentences.en: Our second story involves Rachel Winter-Roach, who left her home in England to work on the sunny island of Tobago, in the southern Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 我们的第二个故事关于Rachel Winter-Roach，她离开家乡英国，前往加勒比海南部阳光明媚的多巴哥岛工作。

sentences.en: Here, Rachel explains some of the food challenges she faced to BBC World Service programme, 'The Food Chain': When I came out to the Caribbean, I was really in for a shock when it came to flavouring and seasoning food, and seasoning is really, really an integral part of food preparation here.
sentences.zh: 在这里，Rachel向BBC世界频道节目《The Food Chain》解释了她所面临的一些食物挑战：当我来到加勒比海时，在食物调味和加香料方面，我真的受到了很大的冲击，而加香料真的是这里食物准备中不可或缺的一部分。

sentences.en: Here, the seasoning is multiple, multiple layers.
sentences.zh: 在这里，调味是多层叠加的。

sentences.en: It took me a while to get used to it because everybody has their own way of seasoning and their own little tweaks, and there are no quantities, so it really takes a lot of practice, a lot of trial and error, and I think my family did not always appreciate the errors in the trials.
sentences.zh: 我花了一段时间才习惯，因为每个人都有自己调味的方法和自己的小调整，而且没有固定的量，所以这真的需要大量的练习、大量的反复试验，而且我认为我的家人并不总是能欣赏这些试验中的错误。

sentences.en: When Rachel moved to Tobago, she was in for a shock.
sentences.zh: 当Rachel搬到多巴哥时，她大吃一惊。

sentences.en: The phrase to be in for a shock means to be sure of experiencing a surprising or unpleasant situation.
sentences.zh: 短语to be in for a shock的意思是肯定会经历一个令人惊讶或不愉快的情况。

sentences.en: In Rachel's case, the surprise involved seasoning - the salt, herbs and spices added to food to enhance the flavour.
sentences.zh: 在Rachel的例子中，惊喜涉及调味——为增强风味而添加到食物中的盐、草本植物和香料。

sentences.en: In the Caribbean, seasoning is a big deal.
sentences.zh: 在加勒比海，调味是一件大事。

sentences.en: Everyone has their own seasoning recipe, including little tweaks, or small adjustments, which they have added themselves.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有自己的调味秘方，包括他们自己添加的小调整（tweaks），也就是小改动。

sentences.en: It took time for Rachel to develop her seasoning skills, mainly through trial and error - a way of solving problems by trying a number of different methods and learning from the mistakes you make along the way.
sentences.zh: Rachel花了一段时间才培养出她的调味技巧，主要是通过反复试验（trial and error）——一种通过尝试多种不同方法并从一路上的错误中吸取教训来解决问题的方法。

sentences.en: Whether you're fleeing war, starting a new job, or enjoying a cream tea, it seems there's lots to learn about a place from its food, including Britain.
sentences.zh: 无论你是逃离战争、开始一份新工作，还是享用奶油茶点，似乎都可以从一个地方的食物（包括英国）中学到很多东西。

sentences.en: So, I think it's time to reveal the answer to my question, Neil.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想是时候揭晓我问题的答案了，Neil。

sentences.en: Why is the traditional British cream tea controversial?
sentences.zh: 为什么传统的英国奶油茶点会引发争议？

sentences.en: Well, I guessed it was because people disagree about whether cream or jam should go on the scone first.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我猜是因为人们对烤饼上应该先抹奶油还是先抹果酱意见不一。

sentences.en: Which was the correct answer. And anyone who says it's jam first is just wrong!
sentences.zh: 这就是正确答案。而且任何说先抹果酱的人都是错的！

sentences.en: OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learned in this programme, starting with comfort zone, a situation in which you feel comfortable and in control.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我们回顾一下我们在本节目中学到的词汇，首先是“comfort zone”（舒适区），即一个你感到舒适和掌控之中的环境。

sentences.en: To adapt means to change so as to successfully fit in with a new situation.
sentences.zh: “Adapt”（适应）意味着改变以便成功融入新环境。

sentences.en: A staple is a basic and important type of food that is regularly eaten by a large portion of the population.
sentences.zh: “Staple”（主食）是很大一部分人口经常食用的基本且重要的食物类型。

sentences.en: The phrase to be in for a shock means to be guaranteed to experience a surprising or unpleasant situation.
sentences.zh: 短语“to be in for a shock”意为保证会经历令人惊讶或不愉快的情况。

sentences.en: A tweak is a small adjustment to something in order to improve it.
sentences.zh: “Tweak”（微调）是对某事物进行的小幅调整，以对其进行改进。

sentences.en: And finally, if you solve a problem by trial and error, you try a number of different methods and learn from the mistakes you make.
sentences.zh: 最后，如果你通过反复试验（trial and error）解决问题，你会尝试多种不同的方法，并从你犯的错误中吸取教训。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, and remember to join us again, here at 6 Minute English.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟又到了，记得再次加入我们，就在《6 Minute English》。

sentences.en: Goodbye for now! Bye!
sentences.zh: 先到这里！拜拜！
